chain: Bigger muscle pump, more blood flow
arginine-aakg.text: Lifters take AAKG before training as a pre-workout 'pump' ingredient, hoping for fuller-looking muscles and better training output that adds up to more size over time. Small human trials have tested strength and performance rather than visible muscle size.

bcaa.text: Lifters use BCAA powders around training to support muscle growth and cut soreness, so they can train more often and build a more muscular physique. The leucine mechanism is well described; trials of stand-alone BCAA supplements for muscle gain are limited.

chain: Zinc and magnesium for sleep and T
zma.text: Bodybuilders take ZMA at night in the hope of better sleep and higher testosterone, which they link to recovery and muscle gain. The few studies on those outcomes in trained athletes give conflicting results.

beef-organ-beef-juice-extract.text: Beef organ and beef juice products are promoted as nutrient-dense support for muscle, so users can recover well and build a stronger physique. Evidence comes mainly from general nutrition knowledge about meat and offal; product-specific trials on muscle are thin.

dimethylglycine-dmg.text: DMG is sold for endurance, oxygen use and immune support, and users take it hoping for quicker recovery and more consistent training. Trials in other conditions have been small, and none examine appearance or training outcomes.

magnesium-glycinate.text: Magnesium glycinate is popular in looksmaxxing circles for sleep, relaxation and recovery, which users tie to a more rested face and better training. Sleep claims often rest on magnesium in general or on stacks with theanine and GABA, with few glycinate-specific trials.

magnesium-malate.text: Magnesium malate is promoted for energy, muscle soreness and recovery, so users can train more often in pursuit of a better physique. Direct human evidence for those uses is thin, with most claims coming from supplement sellers.

inositol-nicotinate.text: Inositol nicotinate is taken as a no-flush form of niacin, with users linking niacin to skin health and a healthier complexion. It has been studied for circulation in conditions such as intermittent claudication; nothing has been published on appearance.

pyridoxamine.text: Longevity and skin-focused users take pyridoxamine as an AGE inhibitor, on the theory that less glycation keeps collagen supple and slows visible skin ageing. It has been studied in diabetic kidney disease; no appearance research exists.

d-ribose-l-cysteine.text: DRLC is marketed to raise glutathione, and users in longevity and skin circles hope for antioxidant protection that supports a healthier, younger look. Research is preclinical or on other conditions; nothing covers appearance.

eutropoflavin-7-8-dhf.text: 7,8-DHF is used by nootropic enthusiasts as a BDNF mimic for mood, cognition and recovery, with no direct appearance link drawn beyond general wellbeing. It has been studied in animals; no human studies exist.

5-htp-oxitriptan.text: In looksmaxxing circles 5-HTP is discussed as a serotonin precursor taken for mood and sleep, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. Many trials cover mood and sleep; none address appearance.

l-tryptophan.text: In looksmaxxing circles L-tryptophan is discussed as a serotonin and melatonin precursor taken for sleep and mood, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. Sleep evidence is mixed, and appearance outcomes have not been studied.

ramelteon.text: In looksmaxxing circles ramelteon is discussed as a prescription melatonin-receptor sleep aid for trouble falling asleep, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied for insomnia in small medical trials; appearance has not been studied.

tasimelteon.text: In looksmaxxing circles tasimelteon is discussed as a prescription circadian-rhythm drug used to align the sleep-wake cycle, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied for non-24-hour disorder and Smith-Magenis sleep problems; appearance has not been studied.

agomelatine.text: Agomelatine is a melatonin-linked antidepressant that some users consider for sleep and mood, on the theory that better sleep and lower stress show up in the face. It is studied for depression; appearance has not been studied.

hydroxyzine.text: In looksmaxxing circles hydroxyzine is discussed as a sedating antihistamine used for anxiety, itch and sleep, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied for anxiety and itch; its effect on looks has not been studied.

low-dose-doxepin-silenor.text: In looksmaxxing circles low-dose doxepin is discussed as a prescription option for staying asleep through the night, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied for sleep-maintenance insomnia; appearance has not been studied.

suvorexant.text: In looksmaxxing circles suvorexant is discussed as an orexin-blocking prescription sleep drug, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. Insomnia data are solid; appearance has not been studied.

lemborexant.text: In looksmaxxing circles lemborexant is discussed as an orexin-blocking prescription sleep drug (Dayvigo), on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied only for insomnia; no appearance studies exist.

daridorexant.text: In looksmaxxing circles daridorexant is discussed as an orexin-blocking prescription sleep drug (Quviviq), on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied for insomnia; no appearance research exists.

eszopiclone.text: In looksmaxxing circles eszopiclone is discussed as a prescription Z-drug sleeping pill (Lunesta), on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied for insomnia; appearance has not been studied.

zaleplon.text: In looksmaxxing circles zaleplon is discussed as a short-acting prescription Z-drug for falling asleep, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied for insomnia; appearance data do not exist.

zopiclone.text: In looksmaxxing circles zopiclone is discussed as a prescription Z-drug sleeping pill, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. Some forum posters claim sleeping pills lower sleep quality over time; it is studied for insomnia, and appearance has not been studied.

temazepam.text: In looksmaxxing circles temazepam is discussed as a prescription benzodiazepine for short-term insomnia, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied for sleep; appearance has not been studied.

gabapentin.text: In looksmaxxing circles gabapentin is discussed as an off-label sleep aid, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is proven for nerve pain and seizures, and its looks effects are untested.

pregabalin.text: Forum posters take pregabalin to lower social anxiety and inhibition, hoping to come across as more relaxed and confident. It is approved for nerve pain, fibromyalgia and seizures; that social use is untested.

mirtazapine.text: Mirtazapine is used off-label for sleep, and some users, such as those trying to gain weight, value its appetite boost. It is approved for depression; its effects on looks are untested.

sodium-oxybate-ghb.text: In looksmaxxing circles sodium oxybate is discussed as a prescription drug that deepens slow-wave sleep, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is approved for narcolepsy; use for looks is untested.

prazosin.text: In looksmaxxing circles prazosin is discussed as an off-label option for trauma-related nightmares that disrupt sleep, on the theory that better sleep shows up as clearer skin, less puffiness and a more rested face. It is studied for blood pressure and PTSD nightmares; nothing links it to appearance.
